--- title: "08 — DARM calibration via Pintelon–Schoukens" description: "The same multisine pipeline applied to the gravitational-wave readout: one Pcal multisine recovers the DARM response R(f) and the sensing function C leakage-free, per-stage drives recover the actuation strengths, and a swept sine is run head-to-head on the same twin." image: thumbnails/08.svg categories: [calibration, closed-loop, DARM] freeze: true --- ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"} ## What you'll learn - The multisine pipeline applied to the **gravitational-wave readout** (DARM). - Recovering the sensing function `C` and per-stage actuation `κ`, leakage-free, under disturbance + readout noise. - **How the 1σ on every calibration parameter converges** — as `1/√T`, onto the Cramér–Rao bound. - **Hierarchical actuation across the quad** (M0/PUM/TST), the inter-stage crossovers, and the **calibration lines at their real height in the DARM spectrum** — with per-line SNR and the strength precision they buy. ::: [![Launch in Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/CaltechExperimentalGravity/system_ident/HEAD?urlpath=lab/tree/docs/examples/08-darm-calibration.ipynb) · run this page live (no install; the [in-browser demo](interactive.qmd) is instant) The earlier examples identify suspensions. This one identifies the **gravitational-wave readout itself** — the DARM loop a LIGO calibration group characterises every run. The method does not change: a periodic multisine, a leakage-free reference FRF, a measured per-bin noise model, and a Cramér–Rao envelope. Only the plant is new: a closed loop with a sensing function `C`, three-stage actuation `A`, and a digital servo `D`, under **both** process disturbance and readout noise. ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Representative, not a specific interferometer The twin uses representative Advanced-LIGO numbers — a coupled-cavity pole near 360 Hz, a ~77 µs delay, three pendulum-stage actuators, and a UGF≈50 Hz loop. It is a *demonstration* of the measurement, not a calibration of any real instrument. The page is rendered with `freeze: true`. ::: ::: {#77263426 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Setup — import the presentation glue"} import sys, pathlib _p = pathlib.Path.cwd() for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]: if (_c / "docs" / "darm_demo.py").exists() and str(_c / "docs") not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_c / "docs")) if (_c / "darm_demo.py").exists() and str(_c) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_c)) import numpy as np import darm_demo as dd ``` ::: ## The loop and what calibration delivers DARM strain is `h = R·d_err/L` with response `R = (1+G)/C` and open-loop gain `G = A·D·C`. The calibration job is to know `R(f)` — and, underneath it, the sensing `C` and the three actuation strengths — to ~1 % in magnitude and ~1° in phase across the band. ::: {#5d4383f6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="The twin's truth — C, A, G, R"} dd.truth_fig() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## One Pcal multisine — what you'd watch A single periodic multisine injected at Pcal, ramped on and off over 3 s, with the DARM error read out under the loop's real disturbance and readout noise. ::: {#84fd36c5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Raw Pcal measurement — drive in, d_err out"} a = dd.pcal_audit(seed=1) dd.pcal_timeseries_fig(a) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The leakage-free FRF `d_err/x_pc = C/(1+G)` with its per-line coherence, on the analytic truth: ::: {#dbf2fdb3 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Leakage-free FRF + coherence"} dd.pcal_bode_fig(a) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## The deliverable: R(f), model-free Because `d_err/x_pc = C/(1+G)`, the response is simply its reciprocal — `R(f) = 1/FRF`, with no model in the loop. Its CRB envelope falls straight out of the FRF's per-bin error. ::: {#013ebb64 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Recovered R(f) ± CRB vs truth"} dd.response_envelope_fig(a) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Underneath: the sensing function C Multiplying the FRF by the (known, designed) loop factor `(1+G)` exposes the optical sensing `C`; a weighted complex fit returns the optical gain, the coupled-cavity pole, and the delay. ::: {#4615d71a .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Sensing fit — g_C, f_cc, τ"} from IPython.display import display display(dd.sensing_table(a)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Sensing function C — representative truth vs P&S recovery** | sensing parameter | true | recovered | σ (CRB) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | optical gain g_C [ct/m] | 1e+06 | 1e+06 | 3.2e+02 | | cavity pole f_cc [Hz] | 360.00 | 359.93 | 0.18 | | delay τ [µs] | 77.0 | 77.0 | 0.07 | ::: ::: ## The actuation strengths, Pcal as the ruler A Pcal-only measurement cannot separate the three stages (they live inside `G` as a product). Driving each stage in turn and dividing by the Pcal FRF removes `C/(1+G)`, leaving `κ_i N_i` referenced to the absolute Pcal meter — so each `κ` comes back on its own. ::: {#63d1a50b .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Recover κ_U / κ_PU / κ_T"} d = dd.actuation_campaign(seed=2) display(dd.actuation_table(d)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Actuation strengths κ — Pcal as the absolute ruler** | stage | true κ | recovered κ | σ (CRB) | |Δ| | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | UIM | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.00052 | 0.01% | | PUM | 0.400 | 0.400 | 0.00045 | 0.02% | | TST | 0.080 | 0.080 | 0.00084 | 0.26% | ::: ::: ## How fast does each parameter converge? The number a calibration group actually plans around is *exposure* — how long a measurement must run to pin each parameter to a target. Because the estimator is period-averaged, every parameter's variance falls as `1/P` (equivalently `1/T`), and the fit / period-to-period-variance σ **is** the Cramér–Rao bound — so the recovered 1σ tracks the `1/√T` law with no free knob. Below, the six core calibration parameters — sensing `g_C`, `f_cc`, `τ` and the three actuator strengths `κ_UIM`, `κ_PUM`, `κ_TST` — are recovered at `P = 16…128` periods and their fractional 1σ plotted against record length. All six fall parallel to the dashed `1/√T` reference; the vertical spread is just per-parameter SNR (`κ_TST`, the weakest actuator, sits highest). Read off the exposure for a target: e.g. sub-1 % on every strength inside a ~minute-scale record here. ::: {#258ba60a .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="σ(θ)/θ vs record length for every cal parameter, against the CRB"} dd.convergence_fig() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Hierarchical actuation and the crossovers the cal lines measure DARM is actuated on all four quad masses hierarchically: the fast, weak ESD (**TST**) takes the command directly, and two nested offload filters push the low-frequency drive up the chain to the **PUM** and the strong, slow **M0** (top mass). Each stage's DARM-referred authority is `A_i = κ_i · D_i(f) · N_i(f)` — the M0-damped reduced-QUAD compliance `N_i` shaped by the distribution filter `D_M0 = O_A·O_B`, `D_PUM = O_A`, `D_TST = 1`. The offload runs in *force* units, so the compliances carry the hierarchy and `κ_i = 1`. M0 owns the lowest frequencies and hands off up the chain, so adjacent stages cross where their authority is equal — **M0/PUM near `F_PT ≈ 0.5 Hz`, PUM/TST near `F_EP ≈ 10 Hz`**. Those crossovers are exactly what a per-stage calibration line on each actuator measures (see `darm_tv.cal_line_response`). The 0.4–3 Hz peaks are the L1/L2/L3 forest, undamped by the M0-only local loop — the twin's real L1 ETMX damping, faithful to the plant. ::: {#4f4e974b .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Per-stage actuation |A_i(f)| with the M0/PUM and PUM/TST crossovers"} dd.hierarchical_actuation() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Future upgrade — damped quad plants from `ssprescale`"} The M0-damped compliances here are built from the reduced QUAD plus a reproduction of the twin's L1 ETMX M0-only velocity damping. A future upgrade will instead use the **new damped quad plants vendored by the `ssprescale` package** (work in progress) — a properly-scaled, multi-loop (M0 + L1 + L2) damped suspension model — so the in-band compliances and the exact crossover frequencies come from the production damping design rather than a single-loop M0 stand-in. ::: ## The calibration lines in the DARM spectrum In operation the strengths are tracked *continuously* by always-on calibration lines — one per actuation stage, plus a Pcal reference — not swept campaigns. What matters is how far each line stands above the DARM noise, because the per-record strength precision is `σκ/κ ≈ 1/SNR`. Below, one line per stage (M0 low, PUM mid, TST in-band) is injected on the hierarchical twin, the loop is simulated under its length-disturbance + readout floor, and the DARM error is deconvolved back to displacement `x = d_err·(1+G)/C`. The spectrum is a full-record periodogram (resolution `df = 1/T`), so **each line stands exactly its SNR above the floor** — the number read straight off the plot. The floor is `√(disturbance² + (readout/|C|)²)`: flat length noise at low frequency, rising above the cavity pole where readout noise divided by the shrinking `|C|` takes over. Longer integration lifts every line as `√T`. ::: {#81ae2e5d .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Inject per-stage cal lines; simulate + deconvolve to a calibrated DARM spectrum"} cs = dd.cal_line_spectrum() dd.cal_line_spectrum_fig(cs) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#a29368ce .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Per-line height, SNR, and the strength precision it buys"} display(dd.cal_line_table(cs)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Per-stage calibration lines: displacement amplitude, in-record SNR, and the per-record strength precision (≈ 1/SNR). Longer integration scales SNR as √T.** | stage line | f [Hz] | displacement [m rms] | SNR (256 s) | σκ/κ [%] | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | M0 | 0.45 | 0.00239 | 90 | 1.11 | | PUM | 3.00 | 0.00371 | 140 | 0.71 | | TST | 40.00 | 0.00692 | 260 | 0.38 | ::: ::: ## Head-to-head with the swept sine Same twin, same disturbance + readout noise, same total wall-clock. The multisine measures every bin at once; the swept sine spends the clock one frequency at a time, so in equal time it reaches only a handful of frequencies (each tight, because it spends full power there) — and covering the whole band to the same uncertainty costs it ~100× longer. Shown on the same twin, not asserted. ::: {#d63b5732 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="σ(R)/|R| — multisine (whole band) vs swept sine (few points), equal wall-clock"} c = dd.comparison(seed=0) dd.comparison_fig(c) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#9dc27f08 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Where the methods differ"} display(dd.fom_table(c)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Where the multisine method differs for DARM (representative; the efficiency is shown above, not asserted)** | figure of merit | swept sine | P&S multisine | | --- | --- | --- | | Frequencies per measurement | 1 (dwell) | all band bins at once | | Leakage | windowed / settle each point | leakage-free (periodic) | | Noise model | assumed / averaged | per-bin, from period-to-period variance | | Budget allocation | uniform / manual | CRB-optimal (Fisher-matched) | | Loop handling | model out the servo | FRF cancels it (reference-based) | | Time for full-band coverage | ≈99 min | 16 s (one window) | ::: ::: ## Honest gaps This twin is a single DARM loop with a one-pole sensing function. It shows leakage-free recovery of `C`, the per-stage strengths and their CRB convergence, the hierarchical actuation crossovers, and the cal-line SNR budget — but it still holds the strengths static within a record (the drift is tracked in [example 13](13-darm-drift-tracking.qmd), which follows `κ(t)` directly), models SRC detuning / the optical spring only through the detuned-sensing option (not folded in here), and omits the cross-couplings of a real interferometer. The noise floor and line SNRs are *representative*, not a specific instrument state; the real test is to run these injections on the same instrument and compare the `σ(R(f))`-per-hour envelopes — see `notes/darm-calibration-via-pns.md`. ## Roadmap The through-line never changes — a periodic multisine, a leakage-free reference FRF, a maximum-likelihood fit toward the Cramér–Rao bound. Each step below raises the *twin's* fidelity toward a real DARM calibration, keeping that one method. **Done** - **Static single-loop calibration** (this page). Sensing `C`, three-stage actuation `κ`, the response `R(f)` with a measured CRB envelope, and a swept-sine head-to-head on the same twin. - **Round 1 — track a drifting parameter** ([example 13](13-darm-drift-tracking.qmd)). A known slow drift on the ESD strength `κ(t)`, recovered with a Lataire–Pintelon time-basis fit inside an honest CRB band, with resolvability proven by a computed bound rather than eyeballed. **Next — raising fidelity, roughly in order** 1. **Realistic drift** — replace the deterministic profile with a stochastic (GP) wander at a physical correlation time; score the recovery statistically. 2. **SRC-detuning optical spring** — replace the single real sensing pole with an optical biquad parametrized on the physical detuning `φ`, so the DARM pole migrates **real → complex** as `φ` drifts (the crossing stays analytic in `φ`). 3. **Several parameters at once** — the optical gain, the cavity-pole / detuning, and the stage `κ_i` drifting jointly, not one scalar in isolation. 4. **One-shot Lataire–Pintelon fit** — fit the time-basis coefficients directly to the record, alongside today's two-step snapshot form, as a cross-check. 5. **Continuous TDCF lines** — always-on calibration lines tracking `κ(t)` between full sweeps, the operational counterpart to the snapshot campaign. 6. **The actuation / DAC chain** — whitening / de-whitening and coil-driver shaping with a pre-injection saturation check at the DAC, plus ESD charge / voltage limits. 7. **Real filters & couplings** — import real DARM / actuation filter shapes and the interferometer cross-couplings (MIMO), toward a calibration of an actual instrument state. Live-CDS / hardware injection is a separate, later phase. The full design and citations live in `notes/darm-calibration-via-pns.md`.
